classification.reason: Request is a scientific goal or asks for planning without a concrete workflow.

plan.goal: Generate one small de novo soluble protein candidate using ESM3, QC the sequence, fold the candidate with Protenix v2, analyse the predicted structure, and rank the single candidate from aggregated evidence.
assumptions: ESM3 is seeded with a 52-residue helical-biased poly-alanine/charged-residue template; the model refines this at temperature 0.7 with 20 diffusion steps and emits both a generated sequence field and a protenix_input_json artifact used by the downstream folding node.
Small soluble target is interpreted as 40–80 residues, monomeric, no disulfides required, assessed at pH 7.4.

No target fold class, functional site, binding partner, or expression-host constraint was provided; the workflow optimises for predicted structural quality and sequence-level solubility indicators only — rerun with explicit constraints to bias generation.
protenix_v2 runs with msa_backend=none and n_sample=1 for speed; a single seed (101) is sufficient because only one candidate enters the pipeline.
structure_analysis uses the top-scoring Protenix model exposed as best_structure_path and runs DSSP for secondary-structure content.
rank_designs aggregates all upstream job records into a scored list; top_k=1 because exactly one candidate is produced.

success_criteria.candidate_generated: esm3_generate returns a novel sequence distinct from the seed
success_criteria.sequence_qc_complete: seq_qc returns charge, composition, and region annotations at pH 7.4
success_criteria.structure_predicted: fold_candidate returns at least one model with per-residue pLDDT scores
success_criteria.structure_analysed: struct_analysis returns per-residue RSA, secondary-structure, and contact records
success_criteria.ranking_produced: rank node returns a scored list with at least one ranked entry and an aggregate design score
